newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha edges up, demand falls for N+A materia.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha edges up, demand falls for N+A materia.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices edged higher on Wednesday as paraffinic material was supported by higher crude prices and the arbitrage to the U.S., traders said.
But demand for heavier naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) material was dropping due to very poor margins, negative in some cases, for making gasoline, they said.
"For N+A there is not much appetite...but there is not a lot of material around either so it is steady," said one broker.
A Russian cargo was believed to have been sold into NWE late Tuesday at $222 cif, but this was not confirmed. At least one other Russian cargo was expected into NWE by the weekend.
Cargo prices rebounded to about $224/$226 on Wednesday, unchanged from yesterday's late prices.
A trader at a Belgian refinery was offering at least one full range barge at $223 fob, up about $1 from Tuesday. He believed demand in NWE was weakening, based on the price for the Russian cargo.
Traders said prompt NWE demand had not picked up dramatically due to the on-again-off-again closures of Algeria's Skikda port due to bad weather.
Three large cargoes of 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes were waiting to be loaded this week at Skikda, but traders said they all had homes, two into Europe and one to Brazil.
"People are still holding back (because of Skikda) but I don't know how long that will last," the broker said.
"The (NWE) market looks balanced with no cargoes under pressure...There is still the potential arbitrage and slowly cargoes are slipping away," he said.
Dec swaps rose $2 to $224.50/$225.50 and Jan gained $3 to $216.50/$217.50. Feb was up $3 at $208.50/$209.50.
